issue.title: My switch skips right past Register
body: I use a switch that steps through everything on a page I can interact with. On the event page it goes from the logo straight down to "Contact us" at the bottom.
It never stops on "Register for Friday" or the dinner menu link, so I can't register or check the food options.

task.instruction: Switch access moves through the same elements as the Tab key. Select "Move focus into the page", then Tab down to "Contact us" in the footer and press Enter. Did you stop on Register on the way?
task.afterReproduce: Register and the menu link were skipped completely. They look clickable but they're a div and a span. Make them real controls.

options.label: Add tabindex="0" to the div
options.feedback: It can receive focus now, but Enter and Space do nothing, and a screen reader doesn't announce it as a button.

options.label: Add role="button" and tabindex="0" to the div
options.replace: Register for Friday
options.feedback: Now it's announced as a button, but it still ignores Enter and Space. You would have to write that keyboard handling yourself. A native button does it for free.

options.label: Change it to a <button>
options.feedback: A native button is focusable, works with Enter and Space, and is announced as a button. All without extra code.

options.label: Change it to <a> without an href
options.feedback: An <a> without an href isn't a link at all to the browser. It still can't be reached with Tab.

options.label: Change it to <a href="#menu">
options.replace: See the dinner menu
options.feedback: The checks pass and it works, but it's announced as a link even though it doesn't go anywhere. It shows and hides content, which is a button's job.

options.label: Change it to a <button> with aria-expanded
options.replace: <button type="button" class="link" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="menu" onclick="showMenu(this)">See the dinner menu</button>
options.feedback: A button that shows and hides content, and aria-expanded tells screen reader users whether the menu is open.

merged.headline: Every control is reachable now.
merged.reply: My switch stops on Register now, and I can open the menu. Registered, and the soup sounds great.
learn: If it does something when clicked, use a <button>. If it goes somewhere, use <a href>.
tabindex and role only change how something is announced; they don't add keyboard behavior.
Switch, voice and keyboard users all depend on real, focusable controls.
